newsitem.title: CANADA: NorTel shrs fall despite beating forecasts.
newsitem.headline: NorTel shrs fall despite beating forecasts.

text.p: Northern Telecom Ltd shares fell in New York and Toronto on Monday, despite an unexpectedly strong fourth quarter earnings performance.
"I don't really know why it's falling," UBS Securities telecommunications analyst Nikos Theodosopoulos said.

"Bookings were very strong, even if you take out the bookings for CDMA (cell division multiple access) in the U.S. they were very strong. Operating revenues were better than expected, gross margins were better than expected, operating expenses were a little bit higher than expected," he added.
NorTel shares were down 3.00 at 90.60 in moderate dealings on the Toronto Stock Exchange soon after session open. They were off 2-3/8 at 67 in New York.
"Switching was down in the fourth quarter, people may have some concerns about that," Theodosopoulos said.

One analyst, who asked not to be identified, said the only negative in the report was the fact that half of NorTel's earnings and one-third of its sales for 1996 were concentrated in the fourth quarter. But the analyst added that this is not a new trend -- the fourth quarter is always of paramount importance to NorTel.

NorTel's sales rose 20 percent to US$4.19 billion in the fourth quarter of 1996 from US$3.50 billion in the year-ago period. Net earnings per share were US$1.23 versus US$0.98 in the fourth quarter of 1995.
Order input for the fourth quarter was a record US$5.27 billion, a 41 percent increase from the US$3.74 billion in the 1995 fourth quarter.
For 1996, NorTel posted sales of US$12.85 billion, 20 above the US$10.67 billion in 1995. Net earnings were US$2.40 a share compared with US$1.85 a share in 1995.
